body:
`case_study:svb-2023` | 2023-03-10 | tickers: US-SIVBQ | confidence: verified

SVB Financial peaked at ~$760 in Nov 2021 and failed on 10 Mar 2023 after customers tried to pull $42 bn on 9 Mar alone. Deposits had tripled 2019-21 with the VC boom (~$60 bn to ~$190 bn); SVB invested them in long-duration Treasuries/MBS, much of it classified held-to-maturity. At end-2022 unrealised HTM losses were ~$15 bn versus ~$16 bn of equity -- disclosed in the 10-K. ~90%+ of deposits were uninsured (NBER: 92.5%), concentrated in a networked VC/startup client base that was burning cash. 8 Mar: SVB announced a $1.8 bn loss on selling AFS securities and a $2.25 bn capital raise -> run. Visible flags: (1) HTM unrealised loss ~ equity (fair-value equity ~zero); (2) deposit base shrinking through 2022 as startups burned cash; (3) uninsured, concentrated deposits; (4) securities >50% of assets; no hedging of rate risk after removing swaps; (5) no chief risk officer for much of 2022; (6) CEO sold shares two weeks before failure under a pre-set plan. Lesson: for banks, mark the securities book to market and compare with equity; deposit concentration and uninsured share determine run speed. Social-media-era runs are hours, not weeks.

**Lesson:** Fair-value equity and deposit concentration decide bank survival
**Spotted early by:** some short sellers and analysts reading the 10-K HTM footnote
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:lender-blowup-signals`, illustrates -> `insight:avoid-ruin`
